nodes.description: Owner address state variable in Ownable, initialised to msg.sender at deployment and used as the sole authority for onlyOwner-guarded functionality.
Ownable.transferOwnership(address newOwner) guarded by onlyOwner; reassigns the owner state variable.
ERC20 transfer; checks balance via SafeMath.sub then performs unchecked balances[_to] += _value addition (overflow risk).
ERC20 transferFrom; decrements sender balance with SafeMath, performs unchecked addition to recipient and rewrites allowance.
Sets allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _value, exposed to the classic approve race condition.
onlyOwner + canMint minting; performs unchecked totalSupply += _amount and balances[_to] += _amount additions.
onlyOwner burn; unchecked subtraction balances[_addr] -= _amount and totalSupply -= _amount.
Returns an investor fee percentage based on the current block timestamp (now >= 1577836800 / 1546300800), i.e. timestamp-dependent economic logic.
Payable entry point; computes fees from msg.value, triggers token minting and Data balance updates via external calls, and mints WBT to the client.
Recursive/iterative private function walking the parent chain, reading data.statuses and calling data.addBalance and data.addReferralDeposit for each ancestor.
onlyOwner withdrawal; reads client balance, subtracts via Data and then performs _addr.transfer, an external value transfer ordering relevant to reentrancy analysis.
onlyOwner withdrawal of raw contract balance to an arbitrary address via _addr.transfer.
onlyOwner; burns tokens for _addr and transfers the corresponding ether value to _addr.
Payable fallback that reads/updates deposits[msg.sender] and forwards msg.value into refProgram.invest, an external call to a user-controllable contract.
Caller-controlled address used as authentication source (owner init, onlyOwner checks) and as balance/mapping key throughout the token, Data and PChannel logic.
Block timestamp (now) consumed by Investors.getInvestorsFee to determine the applicable investor fee tier.
External interaction pattern: PChannel forwarding value to refProgram.invest and Referral forwarding value to _addr.transfer, both able to hand control to an external party.
Unchecked += / -= arithmetic on token balances and totalSupply (transfer, mint, burn), allowing integer overflow or underflow.
onlyOwner credit of an internal client balance by an arbitrary amount, invoked from the fee distribution path.
onlyOwner debit of an internal client balance; requires balances[_addr] >= amount before subtracting.
Local copy of msg.value inside Referral.invest used as the base for service, referral and investor fee computation.
Address parameter of Ownable.transferOwnership; becomes the new owner.
Recipient address parameter of BasicToken.transfer and StandardToken.transferFrom.
Token amount parameter of BasicToken.transfer used in SafeMath.sub and the unchecked recipient addition.
Source address parameter of StandardToken.transferFrom used to index balances and allowed.
Spender address parameter of StandardToken.approve written into the allowed mapping.
Target address parameter of Referral.withdraw / withdrawOwner / withdrawToken used as recipient of _addr.transfer.
Amount parameter of Referral.withdraw / withdrawOwner / withdrawToken used in the balance require and the value transfer.
Beneficiary address parameter of Referral.invest that receives minted tokens and determines the parent chain via data.parentOf.
Caller-supplied deposit counter in Referral.invest indexing serviceFees and referralFees and controlling the fee branch.
Starting parent address parameter of Referral.distribute; iterated up the referral tree.
Loop index local variable in Referral loops (fee distribution/status update).
Boolean flag parameter of Referral.withdraw selecting between investor balance and client balance.

edges.reason: The owner state variable is initialised directly from msg.sender, making the privileged role caller-determined at deployment.
transferOwnership is gated by onlyOwner, which requires msg.sender == owner.
The newOwner parameter is written into the owner state variable by transferOwnership.
transfer indexes balances[msg.sender] as the source of funds, so the caller controls the debited account.
transferFrom uses msg.sender to look up and decrement allowed[_from][msg.sender].
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender], tying the allowance to the caller.
mint is protected by onlyOwner, requiring msg.sender to be the owner.
burn is protected by onlyOwner, requiring msg.sender to be the owner.
transfer performs balances[_to] += _value without SafeMath, exposing the credit side to integer overflow.
mint performs totalSupply += _amount and balances[_to] += _amount with unchecked arithmetic.
burn performs balances[_addr] -= _amount and totalSupply -= _amount with unchecked arithmetic.
getInvestorsFee branches on the block timestamp (now), creating a timestamp-dependent privilege/fee decision.
Referral.invest consumes the timestamp-derived fee returned by getInvestorsFee, propagating the timestamp dependency into the payout path.
The PChannel fallback forwards value with refProgram.invest.value(...), handing control to an external contract before state is finalised.
The fallback reads and mutates deposits[msg.sender] and forwards msg.value, so the caller drives the external call.
PChannel calls back into Referral.invest, allowing reentry into the fee distribution and minting logic.
invest invokes distribute(data.parentOf(client), 0, depositsCount, amount) to pay the upline.
invest credits the owner through data.addBalance(owner, serviceFee * 10000).
distribute repeatedly calls data.addBalance for each ancestor node in the referral chain.
withdraw debits the client through data.subtrBalance before transferring ether.
withdraw executes _addr.transfer, an external value transfer after balance mutation.
withdrawOwner executes _addr.transfer of raw contract balance to a caller-supplied address.
withdrawToken burns tokens then transfers ether to _addr, mixing state change and external value transfer.
The _to parameter is the recipient whose balance is credited in transfer.
The _value parameter is subtracted from the sender balance via SafeMath.sub and added to the recipient.
The _from parameter is the account debited by transferFrom.
The _spender parameter is the key written in the allowed mapping by approve.
The _addr parameter selects the balance queried and is the destination of the ether transfer in withdraw.
The _amount parameter bounds the withdrawal and is multiplied by 1000000 before the balance subtraction.
The client parameter receives the minted tokens and seeds the parent lookup via data.parentOf(client).
The depositsCount parameter indexes serviceFees and referralFees and selects the fee calculation branch.
The _node parameter is the starting address iterated through the referral tree in distribute.
The loop index i drives the iteration over the referral chain and threshold array in the distribution logic.
The investor flag selects between investorBalanceOf and balanceOf, and between subtrInvestorBalance and subtrBalance.

normalization_plan.reason: The amount local variable is a direct copy of msg.value used only inside invest for fee computation.
The recipient parameter is consumed only by transfer for the balance credit and Transfer event.
The value parameter is consumed only by transfer for the SafeMath subtraction and unchecked credit.
The source parameter is consumed only by transferFrom when indexing balances and allowed.
The spender parameter is consumed only by approve when writing the allowed mapping.
The address parameter is consumed by the withdrawal functions as the balance holder and ether recipient.
The amount parameter is consumed by the withdrawal functions for balance checks and value transfer.
The client parameter is only used by invest to mint tokens and to look up the parent for distribution.
The depositsCount parameter is only used by invest to index fee arrays and select the fee branch.
The node parameter is only used by distribute as the traversal cursor over the referral tree.
The loop index local variable exists solely to iterate the distribution/status-update loops.
The boolean flag parameter is only used by withdraw to choose between investor and client balances.
